results.Notes: Closest bank comparisons MA-Q-0253 (token overlap 0.107) and MA-Q-0271 (stem similarity 0.481); no other question in the 406-item bank cites MA-PHARMACY-SUITABILITY. Materially distinct: the decision is who the suitability factors reach, and the item makes the candidate notice that every factor is framed as 'applicant, licensee, or interest holder' and that the out-of-state and consent-agreement limbs are inside rather than outside the list. Distractors B and C are the two readings a practitioner actually advances for an investor with a clean corporate applicant, and neither is eliminable from wording.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0363 (overlap 0.115, same closure and transfer chapter but a different provision) and MA-Q-0060 (stem similarity 0.411). Materially distinct: this is the only item in the bank turning on the outgoing licensee's own 247 CMR 6.11(1) notice as a duty separate from the buyer's application. The scenario is an ordinary sale of a pharmacy and the seller's reasoning ('the buyer's filing tells the Board everything') is the argument actually made in practice.

Closest comparison MA-Q-0389 (overlap 0.192, stem similarity 0.526), which shares one option verbatim: 'The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances' is keyed in this item at C and in MA-Q-0389 at B. That is the only verbatim option repetition anywhere touching this tranche. The two items also both test who signs the inventory. I have recorded the overlap as a failure against MA-Q-0389 rather than here, because this item carries two propositions unique in the bank, the ten-day attestation window and the flat bar on the transferor possessing controlled substances after the transfer date. The controller may instead reword this item's option C; only one of the pair needs changing.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0293 (overlap 0.125) and MA-Q-0258 (stem similarity 0.413); MA-Q-0368 is the nearest conceptual sibling in tranche, but that is a provisional outsourcing registration under 247 CMR 21.03 while this is a provisional pharmacy licence under 247 CMR 6.17, and the two provisions differ on renewal. The decision is genuinely judgmental: the applicant's substantial compliance and evident progress are exactly what 6.17(1)(b) makes the entry test, and the candidate must see that the entry test is not a ground for more time.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0103 (overlap 0.125) and MA-Q-0340 (stem similarity 0.361); no other bank item cites MA-WHOLESALE-CHANGE-AND-QUALIFICATION. Materially distinct and a realistic compliance-officer conversation. Two propositions must be resolved in one option, which is why the option set is built on 'sound on one, wrong on the other' pairs rather than single assertions; that structure is authentic and not guessable. See the legal record for a separate precision point about attributing the felony conviction to a director.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0339 (overlap 0.117) and MA-Q-0177 (stem similarity 0.383). Materially distinct: this is the only item in the bank that contrasts the wholesale druggist one-year December cycle with the pharmacy and outsourcing facility two-year even-year cycle, and it pairs that with the per-place-of-business rule. Counsel's advice is the advice a group actually receives, and the distractors each concede one limb and deny the other, so none is self-eliminating.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0196 (overlap 0.065) and MA-Q-0274 (stem similarity 0.567, unrelated subject); this is the only nuclear pharmacy item in the bank. The decision is a boundary judgment between nuclear pharmacy and nuclear medicine, which is the live question when a nuclear pharmacy describes its services to a hospital. Distractors B, C and D are each a service the hospital would plausibly ask about and none is eliminable from wording.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0216 (overlap 0.107) and MA-Q-0204 (stem similarity 0.363); MA-Q-0364 is the in-tranche sibling on provisional status but under a different instrument with a different rule. Materially distinct and realistic: an entity awaiting FDA inspection with finished batches on hand is the exact situation 247 CMR 21.03(3) was written for. Distractor B (shipment stays inside the Commonwealth) is genuinely tempting and is defeated only by reading the words 'within or outside'.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0289 (overlap 0.156) and MA-Q-0278 (stem similarity 0.392); no other bank item cites MA-THEFT-LOSS-TAMPERING-REPORT. The item is well built because it separates three things a candidate conflates: the recipient (Drug Control Program, not the Board), the trigger (discovery, not the delivery), and the sufficiency of suspected tampering without a confirmed loss. The Manager of Record's instinct to investigate first is the realistic wrong answer.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0320, which shares MA-PATIENT-PROFILE-DUTY, and MA-Q-0112 (overlap 0.107) and MA-Q-0328 (stem similarity 0.487). Materially distinct from MA-Q-0320: that item tests the reasonable-effort content duty on allergy history, while this tests the unqualified system-capability duty, and the item's whole point is that the reasonable-effort standard does not travel across the paragraph. The overnight-batch scenario is a real system limitation and the pharmacy's 'we ask patients thoroughly' defence is the real argument.

Closest comparison MA-Q-0311, which shares MA-CPA-CONSTITUTION-CURRENCY and whose keyed option C states the biennial review requirement; also MA-Q-0001 (stem similarity 0.410). The two are distinguishable in kind: MA-Q-0311 asks what the definition requires for valid constitution, this asks what follows at twenty-six months, and the trap here is that formation and currency are different questions. I record that a candidate who has met MA-Q-0311 reaches this item's answer quickly; the reverse is not true, and the decision itself (whether to keep co-managing this afternoon) is a genuine practice judgment.

Closest comparison MA-Q-0309, which shares MA-COUNSELING-OFFER-METHOD but tests the third paragraph of s. 21A (toll-free number affixed to the container) rather than the second (method of the offer); also MA-Q-0278 (stem similarity 0.374). Materially distinct. The receipt-line practice and the manager's rationalisation are both real, and the deaf patient makes the candidate apply the needs-based alternative rather than recite it. Distractor E is the weakest of the five, being ethically as well as legally wrong, but the remaining four carry the discrimination.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0324, which shares MA-PROSPECTIVE-REVIEW-MANDATE but tests the mandatory review and its permissive screening menu, and MA-Q-0399 (overlap 0.117) and MA-Q-0340 (stem similarity 0.576). Materially distinct: this is the only item in the bank on the s. 21A setting carve-out, and the mixed hospital with a lobby outpatient window is the fact pattern that makes the carve-out's patient-status basis bite. Distractors A and D are the two 'whole pharmacy' readings a director would actually propose.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0317 (overlap 0.107) and MA-Q-0278 (stem similarity 0.358); no other bank item cites MA-RX-LABEL-PRINTING. The two-day structure is what makes this a judgment rather than a recall item: the same act is lawful on Saturday and unlawful on Monday, and the candidate must locate the trigger rather than the conduct. A Saturday printer failure with patients waiting is an everyday event.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0317 (overlap 0.097) and MA-Q-0328 (stem similarity 0.399); no other bank item cites MA-RX-NDC-RECORDING. Materially distinct. The item is well constructed because the cascade in 247 CMR 9.04(7) is ranked rather than disjunctive, and options A, B and C each embody a different wrong reading of the same sentence (free choice, supply-chain logic, completeness), all of which are things a pharmacist actually says.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0234 (overlap 0.200) and MA-Q-0331 (stem similarity 0.608, unrelated subject); no other bank item cites MA-RX-TELEPHONE-RECEIPT. Materially distinct. The item turns on a genuine reading question, whether the approval clause qualifies the intern as well as the certified technician, and both keyed options are needed to show the candidate has resolved it. The pharmacist being mid-counselling is the ordinary reason the question arises.

FAIL on reasoning_not_trivia. Once 247 CMR 9.04(10) is known the item reduces to adding thirty days to a date; there is no legal judgment to make, no competing provision to reconcile and no facts to characterise. The stem is a frame rather than a situation: it supplies the thirty-day window as a premise, names no drug, schedule or clinical context, and asks only which of four dates is right. Option E is then self-eliminating for anyone who reads the stem, and options A to D enumerate four dates each paired with its own counting convention, so the option set itself teaches the candidate that the whole question is which convention applies. The underlying rule is worth testing and the mpje_trap is real, so the fix is an edit rather than a rewrite: put the convention to work inside a dispensing decision, for example a Schedule II prescription written 1 March and presented on 31 March where the pharmacist must decide whether to dispense, so that the candidate applies 9.04(10) and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 23(a) together rather than reciting a counting rule. The key need not change. Closest comparisons MA-Q-0008 (overlap 0.148) and MA-Q-0001 (stem similarity 0.467); no other bank item cites MA-RX-DATE-COUNTING, so the item is distinct, and I record separately in the legal record that its key is legally correct and that my own blind answer was wrong. Tranche-level observations recorded for the controller rather than against this item: (1) running the repository's own scripts/check_structural_patterns.py unmodified over these 30 items alone returns severity ERROR with two findings, SATA_KEY_CONCENTRATION (key CE occurs 3 of 11 SATA items, against its own 25% threshold) and SATA_CORRECT_COUNT_CONCENTRATION (two-correct occurs 7 of 11, against its own 55% threshold); at the gate's default MA-Q-0011+ scope the same call returns PASS with zero findings, so the concentration is invisible to the release gate. The two-correct rate of 7/11 against 23.4% in the rest of the bank is a one-sided binomial p of 0.0051. (2) Sixteen of the 30 items are drawn from just two instruments, ten from 247 CMR 6.00 and six from consecutive paragraphs of 247 CMR 9.04 ((3), (7), (8), (10), (11) and (14)), so the set reads in places as a section-by-section sweep rather than a spread of practice situations.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0117 (overlap 0.105) and MA-Q-0278 (stem similarity 0.433); no other bank item cites MA-RX-OFFSITE-PROCESSING. Materially distinct and among the strongest items in the tranche: the pharmacist has done everything a careful pharmacist would do, and the item asks whether careful checking of the product substitutes for verification of the process. Central fill from an out-of-state hub is a live Massachusetts compliance question and the Board has a standing policy on it. Distractor D is the classic overgeneralisation and A is the answer most candidates will want.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0353 (overlap 0.115) and MA-Q-0331 (stem similarity 0.528); no other bank item cites MA-RX-CUSTOMER-IDENTIFIER. Materially distinct. The conditions in 247 CMR 9.04(14)(c) are cumulative and the item is built so that the sympathetic fact (a housebound patient, a real hardship) is the trap: the candidate who stops at the hardship belief picks A. Both keyed options are operative steps rather than restatements.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0353 (overlap 0.152) and MA-Q-0284 (stem similarity 0.595). Materially distinct: this is the only bank item that separates the s. 21 container label from the s. 22 prescription contents, and the single false option, the practitioner's registration number, is the exact element candidates migrate between the two lists. I note the four-of-five keyed shape reduces the item to finding the one false statement, which is a legitimate SATA form but a weaker discrimination than a two- or three-correct item; it passes because the false option is genuinely non-obvious.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0001 (overlap 0.125) and MA-Q-0020 (stem similarity 0.409); no other bank item cites MA-RX-LARGE-PRINT-DIRECTIONS. Materially distinct. The two-patient structure carries the reasoning: the same statutory duty is dormant for the elderly patient who says nothing and active for the patient who asks, so the candidate must locate the trigger rather than the protected class. Option E, enlarging the whole label rather than the directions, is a genuine and tempting overreach.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0116, which shares MA-ORAL-CONTROLLED-DOCUMENTATION but tests the Schedule VI carve-out from s. 20(c), and MA-Q-0123 (overlap 0.193) and MA-Q-0020 (stem similarity 0.411). Materially distinct and complementary rather than overlapping: MA-Q-0116 asks what survives when s. 20(c) does not apply, this asks what has failed when it does. The item requires two independent defects to be spotted, which is why the 'only that ...' distractors are effective; each concedes one defect and hides the other.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0067 (overlap 0.130) and MA-Q-0186 (stem similarity 0.460); no other bank item cites MA-CII-PHARMACIST-ENDORSEMENT. Materially distinct. Two omissions must both be found and the scenario supplies a plausible-looking substitute for each, the technician's filing and the label initials, so the distractors that accept one of them are authentic. Option D, a second pharmacist's countersignature, is the only weak option and it is a real cross-state confusion.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0293 (overlap 0.114) and MA-Q-0060 (stem similarity 0.375); no other bank item cites MA-CS-PERSONNEL-SCREENING. Materially distinct. The facts are built to make the lawful answer feel unjust, eleven incident-free years and a documented history, which is precisely what makes 'at any time' the point of the item. Option B, keeping him away from the cage, is the mitigation an employer would actually propose. Option E, a vouching registrant, is the weakest of the five.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0073 (overlap 0.156) and MA-Q-0265 (stem similarity 0.578); MA-Q-0363 is the in-tranche neighbour on closure but tests the controlled substance transfer procedure rather than the notice duties. Materially distinct and the most demanding item in the tranche: three pharmacy types must be run against four provisions and two carve-outs. I note the four-of-five keyed shape and that the single false option, the non-resident post-closure submission, is exactly the carve-out in the closing words of 6.13(6), so the discrimination is real rather than incidental.

Closest comparison MA-Q-0390 (overlap 0.225, the highest pairing in the tranche), also MA-Q-0278 (stem similarity 0.478). The two are a deliberate contrast pair on different provisions, 6.16 relocation against 6.12 name change, and each uses the other's period as a distractor. Materially distinct, though I record that a candidate meeting both in one sitting can use each to eliminate an option in the other. A move two doors along is the fact that makes the item a judgment rather than a lookup.

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0382 (overlap 0.125) and MA-Q-0020 (stem similarity 0.452); MA-Q-0388 is the in-tranche neighbour, both resting on 247 CMR 6.15 but on different paragraphs and different pharmacy types. Materially distinct. The item requires two defects to be found, the timing and the omitted counselling area, and option C is a well-chosen trap because certified blueprints genuinely are required, just of compounding pharmacies under 6.15(4).

Closest comparisons MA-Q-0385 (overlap 0.078) and MA-Q-0265 (stem similarity 0.533); MA-Q-0387 is the in-tranche neighbour on 247 CMR 6.15. Materially distinct: that item is a Drug Store remodel under 6.15(1) and (3), this is a secondary engineering control under 6.15(2) and (4), and each item's wrong answer is the other's rule. The director's like-for-like argument is the argument actually made, and the item is decided by reading 'replacing' in the list of five verbs rather than by reasoning about configuration.

FAIL on distinct_from_bank, against MA-Q-0363 in this same tranche. Option B here, 'The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances', is character-for-character identical to option C of MA-Q-0363 and is keyed correct in both; it is the only verbatim option repetition anywhere touching this tranche. The overlap is not confined to wording: two of this item's three keyed propositions, the inventory scope and who signs the inventory, are also the subject of MA-Q-0363's options C and D, because 247 CMR 6.10(2)(a) and 6.14(2)(a) to (b) are drafted in parallel. A candidate who has met MA-Q-0363 receives two of this item's three decision points free, which is the concern distinct_from_bank exists to catch. This is an edit rather than a rewrite: reword one occurrence so that the two items reach the inventory scope by different routes, for example by testing here whether a Schedule VI product not reportable to the prescription monitoring program is inside the count. The key need not change, and only one of the pair needs changing; I have recorded the pairing in MA-Q-0363's note as well and left that item passing because it carries two propositions unique in the bank. The item is otherwise sound: an amicable departure with a successor identified is the ordinary occasion for the application, options C and D are authentic (the staff-pharmacist substitution and the certified copy are both real practice shortcuts), and 6.10(1)'s appearance power is distinctive. Other comparisons MA-Q-0265 (stem similarity 0.601) and MA-Q-0274, neither related in substance. Tranche-level observations recorded for the controller rather than against this item: (1) running the repository's own scripts/check_structural_patterns.py unmodified over these 30 items alone returns severity ERROR with two findings, SATA_KEY_CONCENTRATION (key CE occurs 3 of 11 SATA items, against its own 25% threshold) and SATA_CORRECT_COUNT_CONCENTRATION (two-correct occurs 7 of 11, against its own 55% threshold); at the gate's default MA-Q-0011+ scope the same call returns PASS with zero findings, so the concentration is invisible to the release gate. The two-correct rate of 7/11 against 23.4% in the rest of the bank is a one-sided binomial p of 0.0051. (2) Sixteen of the 30 items are drawn from just two instruments, ten from 247 CMR 6.00 and six from consecutive paragraphs of 247 CMR 9.04 ((3), (7), (8), (10), (11) and (14)), so the set reads in places as a section-by-section sweep rather than a spread of practice situations.

Closest comparison MA-Q-0386 (overlap 0.225), also MA-Q-0278 (stem similarity 0.472). Distinct provisions as described in MA-Q-0386's note. Materially distinct from the bank: no other item cites MA-PHARMACY-NAME-CHANGE. A rebrand with everything else unchanged is a realistic and easily overlooked notification trigger, and the manager's plan to mention it at renewal is the ordinary error. This is the lowest-difficulty item in the tranche and its distractors are correspondingly thinner, but each names a real alternative regime. Bank-level observation outside this tranche, recorded for the controller: across the 234 SBA items outside this tranche the longest option is the keyed option 153 times (65.4%) against a 20% chance rate, and the mean keyed option runs 97.9 characters against 79.1 for distractors, so picking the longest option scores about 65% on the released SBA bank with no legal knowledge. The repository's SBA_ANSWER_LENGTH_LEAKAGE check does not catch this because it fires only per item when the key is at least 1.6 times the longest distractor and at least 6 tokens longer, which tests outliers rather than the aggregate tendency. This tranche is materially better than the bank on that measure (9 of 19, 47.4%, mean keyed 78.2 against 74.5) but still above chance.
